## Introduction

To check that `pypomp`'s particle filter is doing the same arithmetic as R
`pomp`'s, both are run many times at one fixed parameter vector — the published
MLE that `pomp` ships as `dacca()`'s default — and their log-likelihood
distributions are compared. Nothing varies across replicates except the seed, so
any systematic gap between the two curves is an implementation difference rather
than Monte Carlo noise.

---

## Setup & Data Loading

```{python Environment setup}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from scipy.stats import ks_2samp
from plotnine import ggplot, aes, geom_density, labs

os.environ["JAX_PLATFORMS"] = "cpu"

PY = pd.read_csv(os.path.join("results", "gpu", "pfilter_logliks.csv"))["logLik"].values
R = pd.read_csv(os.path.join("results", "R", "pfilter_logliks.csv"))["logLik"].dropna().values

py_meta = ru.load_json(os.path.join("results", "gpu", "latest.json"))
r_meta = ru.load_json(os.path.join("results", "R", "latest.json"))
```

---

## Likelihood Evaluation at the MLE

### Kolmogorov-Smirnov (KS) test

```{python KS test}
ks_stat, ks_p = ks_2samp(PY, R)

ks_table = pd.DataFrame({
    "Source": ["pypomp (GPU)", "R pomp"],
    "Replicates": [len(PY), len(R)],
    "Mean": [np.mean(PY), np.mean(R)],
    "SD": [np.std(PY, ddof=1), np.std(R, ddof=1)],
    "Min": [np.min(PY), np.min(R)],
    "Median": [np.median(PY), np.median(R)],
    "Max": [np.max(PY), np.max(R)],
})

display(HTML(ks_table.round(3).to_html(classes="table table-striped table-hover", index=False)))
print(
    f"Mean difference: {np.mean(PY) - np.mean(R):+.4f} nats\n"
    f"Two-sample KS:   D = {ks_stat:.4f}, p = {ks_p:.4g}"
)
```

---

### Density comparison

```{python Density plot, fig.width=8, fig.height=5}
df = pd.concat([
    pd.DataFrame({"logLik": PY, "source": "python"}),
    pd.DataFrame({"logLik": R, "source": "R"}),
], ignore_index=True)

(
    ggplot(df, aes(x="logLik", fill="source", color="source"))
    + geom_density(alpha=0.3)
    + labs(
        title="Log-likelihood density at the MLE: pypomp vs R pomp",
        subtitle="Monte Carlo variation across identical independent evaluations",
        x="Log-Likelihood", y="Density", fill="Source", color="Source",
    )
    + ru.scale_fill_premium()
    + ru.scale_color_premium()
    + ru.theme_premium
)
```

::: {.callout-note}
### Expectation
The two densities should overlap heavily. A KS test that fails to reject is the
positive result here; a visible shift in location would point at a difference in
the transition process or the measurement model rather than at sampling noise.
:::
